diagnosis.cause: No leadKaneFinding/failing screenshot was provided, so the primary evidence is absent; the strongest observed root cause is the secondary-friction loop where Kane repeatedly clicked the noon slot and then had to handle the surprise picker, e.g. “click: PRIMARY: noon time slot…” followed by “select: Select "Downtown" in "Gym"” and then another noon click.
patterns: Blocking overlays: a full-page cookie/consent iframe locks scroll until answered.
A consent modal inside an iframe that traps focus and locks page scroll until answered.
Two overlapping modals where the lower one, location access, must be accepted but a newsletter modal covers it.
A required location picker that pops up mid-flow.
A time-slot picker drawn on a canvas with no DOM nodes as the visible control.
Custom controls: visible canvas time slots plus indirect hidden radios, and modal-driven location selection.
The submit button is three screens down past filler content.
A confirmation appears 4 seconds after submit.
changes: First, because there is no leadKaneFinding, preserve the working human path but remove the largest secondary loop: replace the “Gym location” read-only text and surprise `#location-picker` modal with an inline native `<select id="gym" name="gym">` inside the booking form, keeping the Downtown option and the same visual field styling.
Update `chooseTime()` so selecting `12:00` no longer opens `#location-picker`; it should simply set `time`, check the matching radio, redraw/update the visible state, and update `#time-chosen`.

Remove or disable the `#location-picker` markup and its `#gym-save` event dependency, or leave it hidden but unused; set `gym` from the inline select’s `change` event and validate against that value on submit.

Replace the visible `<canvas id="slots">` arrival-time picker with visible native radio labels/buttons for 9am, 12pm (noon), and 6pm, styled to match the existing `.time` pill design. Keep the accessible text “12pm (noon)” so Kane can target the requested noon slot directly.

Move the `Confirm my free visit` submit button directly after the waiver checkbox, before the long `.filler` informational sections, so it is not three screens below the required fields. Keep the filler content below the form if desired for the same page tone.

Simplify the booking entry overlays: when `#book` is clicked, show the booking form directly or show only one real, labeled location/permission dialog—not the overlapping newsletter plus location stack. If the prompt is kept, make `Accept` immediately open the form without requiring the newsletter to be dismissed first.

Convert the consent iframe to an in-page, non-iframe dialog or compact cookie bar with real buttons, preserving the “Accept all”/privacy copy but avoiding focus trapping and body scroll lock. Kane already passes this sometimes, so this is secondary after the location/time loop.

Keep the confirmation `#confirmation` as persistent DOM content with `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"`, keep the exact reference `PL-5519`, and do not auto-hide it. The existing 4-second delay is acceptable only if the fresh run waits; reducing it to about 1 second would remove another known friction point while still showing PL-5519 for at least five seconds afterward.
diagnosis.acceptanceCheck: A fresh Kane run should navigate, accept/dismiss consent, open the booking form, enter Sam Rivera / sam@example.com / 2026-11-02, select Downtown inline, select 12pm/noon once, tick the waiver, submit without any surprise picker or repeated noon clicks, and observe a persistent booking confirmation containing PL-5519 that remains visible for at least five seconds.
